title: Closed scheme-theoretic unions are pushouts
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $Y,Z\hookrightarrow X$ closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $W=Y\cup Z$ be their scheme-theoretic union [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-union], defined by the intersection of their ideal sheaves, and let $E=Y\times_X Z$ be their scheme-theoretic intersection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then the inclusions make $W$ the pushout [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of $Y\leftarrow E\to Z$ in the category of schemes. Explicitly, for any scheme $T$, morphisms $Y\to T$ and $Z\to T$ which agree on $E$ extend to a unique morphism $W\to T$. On an affine open of $X$ with coordinate ring $R$ and ideals $I,J$ for $Y,Z$, the corresponding ring identity is $R/(I\cap J)\cong (R/I)\times_{R/(I+J)}(R/J)$. No reducedness, Noetherianity or separatedness is required.

source.place: Tag 0C4J, lemma-scheme-theoretic-union: the cocartesian square and its affine-local proof.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ and write $Y_U=Y\times_XU$, and likewise $Z_U,W_U,E_U$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $Y_U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ and $Z_U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ for ideals $I,J\subseteq R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-union], $W_U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/(I\cap J))$, with the closed inclusions from $Y_U,Z_U$. Their affine ring maps are the canonical quotients: the composite $R\to R/(I\cap J)\to R/I$ is $R\to R/I$, and $R\to R/(I\cap J)$ is surjective, so it determines $R/(I\cap J)\to R/I$ uniquely; the same applies to $R/J$. The pullback universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $E_U$ with $Y_U\times_UZ_U$: both represent pairs of maps into $Y,Z$ with equal composites into $X$ and a common factorization into $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], this is $\operatorname{Spec}((R/I)\otimes_R(R/J))$. Identify this tensor product with $R/(I+J)$ by $[a]\otimes[b]\mapsto[ab]$, with inverse $[r]\mapsto[r]\otimes1$. The inverse is well-defined because $I$ kills the first factor and $[j]\otimes1=1\otimes[j]=0$ for $j\in J$; the balancing relation shows both composites are identities. Under this identification the projections from $E_U$ are induced by $R/I\to R/(I+J)$ and $R/J\to R/(I+J)$.

source.place: Tags 0C4J (lemma-scheme-theoretic-union), affine chart, and 0C4I (lemma-scheme-theoretic-intersection), its tensor-quotient calculation.

proof.text: The canonical ring homomorphism $\theta:R/(I\cap J)\to (R/I)\times_{R/(I+J)}(R/J)$ sends $[r]$ to $([r],[r])$. Its kernel is zero since a representative mapping to zero lies in both $I$ and $J$. Given a compatible pair $([a],[b])$, write $a-b=i+j$ with $i\in I$, $j\in J$. Then $c=a-i=b+j$ maps to that pair, proving surjectivity. Thus $\theta$ is a ring isomorphism. It commutes with both projections by its displayed formula, proving the ring-identity clause with its canonical maps. This calculation also applies when a quotient is the zero ring.

proof.text: Let $T$ be any scheme and $f:Y\to T$, $g:Z\to T$ agree on $E$. Set $A=R/I$, $D=R/(I+J)$, $B=R/J$ and $P=A\times_D B$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-closed-pinching-pushout] with its ring named $T$ equal to $B$, and its target scheme named $Z$ equal to our $T$. The required map $A\twoheadrightarrow D$ is surjective: every class $[r]$ in $D$ is the image of $[r]$ in $A$. The other map $B\to D$ is the canonical quotient, allowed by the cited statement without any extra condition. Step 2 gives $R/(I\cap J)\cong P$, commuting with both projections; functoriality in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives the compatible isomorphism $W_U\cong\operatorname{Spec}P$. Step 1 identifies the overlap and its two maps with $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}A,\operatorname{Spec}B$. Thus the cited universal property in all schemes gives a unique $h_U:W_U\to T$ extending $f|_{Y_U},g|_{Z_U}$. This works for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, including empty charts and zero quotient rings.

proof.text: The opens $W_U$ for affine opens $U\subseteq X$ cover $W$, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Here $W_U$ is the inverse image of $U$ under the closed immersion $W\to X$, so the covering assertion follows by taking inverse images of the affine-open cover of $X$. Given two such opens from $U,V$, cover $U\cap V$ by affine opens $B\subseteq U\cap V$, using that same basis statement; no affineness of $U\cap V$ is assumed. Taking inverse images gives $W_U\cap W_V=W\times_X(U\cap V)=\bigcup_B W_B$. The analogous inverse-image identities for $Y,Z$ identify their restrictions inside every $W_B$ with $Y_B,Z_B$. On $W_B$, both $h_U|_{W_B}$ and $h_V|_{W_B}$ have the prescribed restrictions $f|_{Y_B}$ and $g|_{Z_B}$. Uniqueness in Step 3, applied to the affine open $B$ of $X$, makes the two morphisms equal. The $W_B$ cover $W_U\cap W_V$, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] makes $h_U,h_V$ agree on that whole overlap. Applying the existence assertion of this gluing lemma to the open cover $(W_U)_U$ gives a morphism $h:W\to T$ restricting to every $h_U$.

source.place: Tag 0C4J, lemma-scheme-theoretic-union: construction is affine-local on the union; Schemes Tags 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens) and 01JB (lemma-glue), mapping property.

proof.text: Take the global closed inclusions $a:Y\to W$ and $b:Z\to W$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-union]. Their affine restrictions are the quotient-induced inclusions of Step 1. On every $E_U$, the two composites into $W$ agree: their ring maps send $[r]\in R/(I\cap J)$ to the same $[r]\in R/(I+J)$. The opens $E_U$ cover $E$, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives the global cocone condition. The composites $h\circ a$ and $f$ agree on every $Y_U$ by Step 3; those opens cover $Y$, so the same equality criterion gives $h\circ a=f$. Likewise $h\circ b=g$ on the cover $(Z_U)_U$. For any other extension $h':W\to T$, Step 3 gives $h'|_{W_U}=h_U$ on every affine chart, and gluing uniqueness gives $h'=h$. These are exactly the cocone and universal properties of the colimit of the finite span [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No reducedness, Noetherianity or separatedness was used; zero rings and empty covers include the empty cases.
